title: The flight into Egypt (Matthew 2:13–23)
hook: the holy family become refugees, fleeing a king's violence by night

segments.voice: Yesterday, the magi: stargazers who followed a light, knelt before a child, and went home another way. Follow the star you have.

A family packs in the dark. No time for goodbyes. Whatever fits in their arms, and a child who doesn't understand why he's been woken. They leave before sunrise, heading for a border, because staying means someone they love may be killed. That happens somewhere in the world tonight. In Matthew's Gospel it happens to Mary, Joseph and the child. The magi have gone home another way, and Herod, the king who asked where the child was, has worked out that he's been tricked. And Joseph has another dream.
screen: `PACKING IN THE DARK.` → `HEROD HAS BEEN TRICKED.` → `JOSEPH DREAMS AGAIN.`

segments.voice: The angel's words are urgent: "Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him." Joseph does it that same night. He never speaks a single word in the Gospels. He just gets up and goes. Then comes the darkest scene in the Christmas story. Herod, furious, orders every boy of two and under in and around Bethlehem to be killed. Matthew is the only source for this; no other writer of the time mentions it, though Herod was known to be ruthless, even with his own sons. Matthew quotes the prophet Jeremiah: "Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not." The story doesn't hurry past the grief. Churches still keep a day for these children, the Holy Innocents, in the days after Christmas. And Egypt, the old land of slavery in the Exodus story, is now the place of safety. Matthew quotes another prophet, Hosea: "Out of Egypt have I called my son." Israel's story, lived again in one child. Coptic Christians in Egypt still trace the places they say the family stayed, and celebrate its arrival every year. Then Herod dies, Joseph dreams again, and they come home, not to Bethlehem but to a small town in Galilee called Nazareth. Before he preached, before he healed, before anyone knew his name, Jesus was a child carried across a border by night.
screen: `ARISE, AND FLEE INTO EGYPT.` · `RACHEL WEEPING FOR HER CHILDREN.` · `OUT OF EGYPT HAVE I CALLED MY SON.` · `HOME TO NAZARETH.` · then, large: `A CHILD CARRIED ACROSS A BORDER BY NIGHT.`

segments.voice: Think of one family that has had to leave home, someone you know, someone you saw in the news, or your own family a generation or two back, and picture them clearly: the packing, the road, the first night somewhere strange. If you pray, pray for them by name, or for the family whose name you'll never know; if you don't, just keep them in mind with care.
Holy Innocents. The name churches still use for the children Herod had killed in and around Bethlehem, grieved in Matthew's Gospel and remembered every year after Christmas.
Your line: he was a refugee first. Before the sermons, the road. Day forty-five, done.

screen: `DAY 45 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE BOY IN THE TEMPLE.`

howItsDone: Many churches remember the flight into Egypt in the days after Christmas, along with the Holy Innocents, and many Christian charities point to this story in their work with refugees. Coptic Christians celebrate the Holy Family's arrival in Egypt each year and visit places tradition links to their journey.

original.note: Greek: flee! The angel's command to Joseph, a cousin of the Latin fugere that gave English fugitive.

trapdoor: what you thought: a quiet trip on a donkey in a Christmas painting.
what it means: a family fleeing a king's violence by night, becoming refugees before the child could walk far.
what a scholar hears: Matthew tells it as Israel's story lived again, into Egypt and called out of it, and he alone records the killing of the children, which no other writer of the time mentions.

sources.ref: Antiquities of the Jews, books 16–17 (Herod's executions of his sons)

notes: The massacre of the innocents is recorded only in Matthew; the script says no other writer of the time mentions it and that Herod was known for ruthlessness, including executing his own sons (Josephus). Confirm the phrasing.
'Joseph never speaks a word in the Gospels' — no words of Joseph are recorded; confirm.
Holy Innocents: December 28 in Western churches, December 29 in many Orthodox churches. The script says 'in the days after Christmas'.
Coptic Orthodox Church: feast of the Entry of the Holy Family into Egypt (24 Pashons, about June 1) and the pilgrimage sites along the traditional route. Confirm.

The carry 'he was a refugee first' is modern language; many churches (e.g., the Catholic apostolic constitution Exsul Familia, 1952) describe the Holy Family as refugees. Keeper may want to confirm the framing.
Original: φεῦγε (imperative of φεύγω, Matthew 2:13). The note links it loosely to Latin fugere via 'fugitive'; they are cognates. Confirm or simplify.
